walkthrough_label: STACKED CASE S1-A - diabetes medicine mix-up: low sugar, an SGLT2 inhibitor taken today and poor long-term control, with raised BP
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mr Imran Siddiqui, 58, is booked for keyhole gallbladder removal. He is slightly pale and sweaty and says he feels a bit shaky and hungry. Glucose 3.6. BP 174/102, repeat 172/100.

history.answer: I am here for my gallbladder, but I feel a bit shaky and hungry.
No chest pain. Sweaty, shaky and hungry now. I walk 2 km.
Type 2 diabetes for nine years; high blood pressure for six years; gallstones. My last HbA1c was about a year ago.
Metformin, gliclazide, dapagliflozin, amlodipine and ramipril. I took all my morning tablets as usual - I forgot about the instructions.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.

observations.note: BP 174/102, repeat 172/100 (below 180/110); HR 96 scores 1; NEWS2 1, which does not detect low glucose.
After the low sugar is treated: glucose 5.8, symptoms gone; repeat BP 172/100.

examination.finding: Slightly pale and sweaty, fully alert and orientated, talking normally.
Mild tenderness under the right ribs.

results.comment: Hypoglycaemia corrected; recheck every 30 to 60 minutes while fasting
Mildly raised (0.6 to 1.5): fasting plus the SGLT2 inhibitor; recheck, venous gas if 1.5 or more
Long-standing high blood pressure; note (picture result)

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: Heart rate 96 scores 1; NEWS2 does not detect low glucose

problems.label: Hypoglycaemia (glucose 3.6) from a sulfonylurea taken while fasting
problems.why: Disability (D in ABCDE): it can deteriorate within minutes to confusion or a seizure, and is quick and simple to treat. The scariest-looking number (BP 172/100) is not the most urgent; the glucose of 3.6 is.
expected_actions: Hypoglycaemia protocol by the nurse now, recheck at 10 to 15 minutes
Ask exactly what he took this morning
Tell the anaesthetist: oral glucose changes the fasting

problems.label: SGLT2 inhibitor taken today; ketones 0.9: risk of ketoacidosis even with a normal sugar
problems.why: Risk of euglycaemic DKA during fasting and surgery; it needs monitoring, and surgery today is unlikely to proceed (the anaesthetist decides). UK 2025 consensus: omit it the day before and the day of surgery.
expected_actions: Check the exact drugs and times
Tell the anaesthetist and the senior

problems.label: HbA1c 76 above the limit of 69 for planned surgery
problems.why: Not dangerous today, but a recognised reason to optimise before planned surgery (CPOC).
expected_actions: Send an HbA1c (none in the last 3 months)
Refer for diabetes optimisation before rebooking

problems.label: Blood pressure 174/102, repeat 172/100 (below 180/110)
problems.why: Below the AAGBI/BHS 180/110 threshold: on its own it would not stop surgery; it needs GP follow-up.

options.text: Hypoglycaemia: ask the nurse to start the hypoglycaemia protocol now, recheck at 10 to 15 minutes, and tell the anaesthetist
options.consequence: Recheck 5.8, symptoms resolve; the fasting status changes (oral glucose), so the anaesthetist must decide.

options.text: Focus on the BP of 172/100 first
options.consequence: Nurse: "His sugar is 3.6." Treatment is delayed and he becomes confused at 15 minutes (glucose 2.9).

options.text: Give him a glucose drink and tell nobody
options.consequence: The anaesthetist discovers it later: an undeclared fasting breach, so the list is re-timed or cancelled.

decisions.prompt: "I took all my tablets": gliclazide and dapagliflozin this morning. What now?

options.text: Check the exact drugs and times and the capillary ketones; tell the anaesthetist
options.consequence: Ketones 0.9: surgery today is not appropriate per guidance.

options.text: Treat the low sugar but send him to theatre
options.consequence: The anaesthetist asks about medicines at Sign In: SGLT2 inhibitor and fasting, ketoacidosis risk. The case is stopped at Sign In.

options.text: Raised but below 180/110: repeat after rest, document, and tell the anaesthetist in the same call; not a reason by itself to cancel
options.consequence: Repeat 172/100: nothing changes today; GP follow-up.

options.text: Cancel the operation for the BP alone and ignore the glucose
options.consequence: Wrong reasoning: the low sugar is not recognised and the glucose falls further.

decisions.prompt: No HbA1c in the last 3 months. What now?

options.text: Send an HbA1c and wait for the result
Skip it because the operation is booked
options.consequence: Whether his diabetes is fit for planned surgery stays unknown.

options.text: SBAR to the senior and the anaesthetist proposing deferral
options.consequence: The team defers surgery and rewrites the diabetes plan: rebook after optimisation.

options.text: Proceed because the BP is below 180/110
options.consequence: The diabetes problems are the reason to defer.

correct: SBAR to the anaesthetist and senior
Deferral, diabetes plan and GP letter

incorrect.shows: Nurse: "His sugar is 3.6."; he becomes confused at 15 min (glucose 2.9)
incorrect.recovery: Treat the hypo now; re-prioritise using ABCDE

incorrect.mistake: Treats the hypo but sends him to theatre
incorrect.shows: The anaesthetist at Sign In asks about medicines; the case is stopped at Sign In

incorrect.mistake: Cancels for the BP alone and ignores the glucose
incorrect.recovery: Use the AAGBI/BHS rule; treat the glucose

incorrect.mistake: Orders a glucose drink without telling the anaesthetist
incorrect.shows: The anaesthetist discovers it later; re-timing or cancellation

missed: Glucose 3.6 not noticed: he becomes quieter; nurse: "He's not making sense"; glucose 2.4, confused; emergency hypo treatment
recovery: Recognises the miss, calls for help; the nurse starts the protocol; glucose recovers; full medication review; correct deferral and plan

recognised: A BP below 180/110 is not itself a reason to cancel
missed: The medication history (what was taken today)
debrief.why_priority: It threatens brain function within minutes and is easily reversed.
debrief.related: Hypoglycaemia, the SGLT2 inhibitor and the HbA1c: all diabetes-management problems
debrief.independent: The BP (related only by shared risk factors)
debrief.trigger_escalation: Any glucose below 4.0 and any SGLT2 inhibitor taken on the day
debrief.if_ignored: A seizure or coma from hypoglycaemia; ketoacidosis during or after surgery
debrief.remember: Check the glucose in every diabetic patient and ask exactly which tablets were taken today.

asa.why: Type 2 diabetes with a low glucose today and blood pressure 174/102: poorly controlled diabetes or blood pressure is ASA 3 in the book's list.
